description: Permutation enumeration over interior points with the chapter's cyclic-hull-order dynamic program.

source.title: Traveling Sales Person with Few Inner Points
source.algorithm_attribution: first fixed-parameter algorithm: enumerate interior-point orders and solve each by dynamic programming
source.implementation_status: clean-room; no book prose or upstream source code copied

input.encoding: [n, k, outer IDs in supplied cyclic hull order, inner IDs, x0, y0, ..., x(n-1), y(n-1)]
input.point_constraint: All coordinates are distinct; outer IDs are the strict convex hull in cyclic order and inner IDs are strictly interior. The geometric classification is supplied, as assumed by the source algorithm.

output.definition: Minimum closed-tour cost among tours respecting the supplied cyclic order of outer points, with each Euclidean edge length rounded to the nearest thousandth (halfway cases downward); this does not claim the exact optimum for unrounded Euclidean distances

workspace.meaning: Bounded point coordinates, distance scratch, two O(k) DP rows, and one interior-point permutation.

contract.outer_order: Use the supplied hull cycle exactly; either orientation and any starting hull vertex are accepted.
contract.permutation_order: Sort interior IDs in ascending order and enumerate their deterministic lexicographic permutations; only the minimum cost is observable.
contract.distance_rounding: For squared integer distance s, compute the nearest integer to sqrt(s*1000^2), rounding an exact tie downward, using integer arithmetic.
